band.name: Litfiba
band.name_origin: Acronym for Località, Italia, Firenze, Via dei Bardi (L-IT-FI-BA). Via dei Bardi 32 was the street address of the band's first rehearsal space in Florence.

history.early_days: Formed in October 1980 in a basement in Via dei Bardi 32, Florence. The band was born in the Florentine underground scene of new wave, post-punk and dark wave. Early influences were British punk and new wave. First live performance was on December 6, 1980 at Rokkoteca Brighton in Florence.
history.first_era: 1980-1989: The 'Trilogy of Power' era. Released Eneide di Krypton (1983), Desaparecido (1985), 17 Re (1986), Litfiba 3 (1988). Lyrics were political and socially conscious. Sound evolved from new wave to more personal rock with Mediterranean influences.
history.second_era: 1989-1999: The 'Tetralogy of Elements' era. Released Pirata (1989), El Diablo (1990), Terremoto (1993), Spirito (1994), Mondi Sommersi (1997), plus live albums Colpo di Coda (1994), Lacio Drom (1995), Croce e Delizia (1998). This was their commercial peak period.
history.third_era: 1999-2009: Piero Pelù left in 1999 due to frictions with Ghigo Renzulli. Gianluigi 'Cabo' Cavallo became new vocalist. Released Infinito (1999), Elettromacumba (2000), Insidia (2001), Essere o Sembrare (2005). Cavallo left in 2006.
history.fourth_era: 2009-2022: Piero Pelù returned. Released Stato Libero di Litfiba (2010), Grande Nazione (2012), Trilogia 1983-1989 (Live 2013), Eutòpia (2016). The 'Trilogy of States' era. Final tour 'Ultimo Girone' in 2022 marked the band's end.

core_members.name: Federico 'Ghigo' Renzulli
core_members.notes: Co-founder and only constant member throughout entire career. Primary composer.

core_members.name: Piero Pelù
core_members.notes: Co-founder. Charismatic frontman. Left in 1999 for solo career, returned in 2009.

past_members.name: Antonio Aiazzi
past_members.notes: Original keyboardist. Left in 1989 when Roberto Terzani switched to bass/keyboards.

past_members.name: Sandro Dotto
past_members.notes: Original vocalist, very briefly, before Pelù joined.

past_members.name: Roberto Terzani
past_members.notes: Replaced Maroccolo on bass. Also played keyboards (replacing Aiazzi) and second guitar.

past_members.name: Federico Poggipollini
past_members.notes: Second guitarist during El Diablo and Terremoto tours.

past_members.name: Candelo Cabezas
past_members.notes: Electronic percussionist. Contributed to Pirata and El Diablo albums.

past_members.name: Franco Caforio
past_members.notes: Drummer during Spirito and Mondi Sommersi era.

past_members.name: Daniele Bagni
past_members.notes: Bassist in the later EMI era.

past_members.name: Gianluigi 'Cabo' Cavallo
past_members.notes: Replaced Piero Pelù. Sang on Elettromacumba, Insidia, Essere o Sembrare. Won 4 gold records.

studio_albums.title: Eneide di Krypton
studio_albums.label: CGD / Warner Music
studio_albums.notes: Soundtrack for theater production. First album. Features instrumental new wave/post-punk.

studio_albums.title: Desaparecido
studio_albums.label: WEA (Warner)
studio_albums.notes: First part of 'Trilogy of Power'. Breakthrough album. Themes of political oppression and Latin American struggles.

studio_albums.title: 17 Re
studio_albums.label: WEA (Warner)
studio_albums.notes: Second part of 'Trilogy of Power'. Most iconic album. Critique of power and corruption. Includes 'Paname', 'Tex', 'Louisiana'.

studio_albums.title: Litfiba 3
studio_albums.label: WEA (Warner)
studio_albums.notes: Third part of 'Trilogy of Power'. Darker, more experimental. Includes 'Dimmi il nome', 'Cangaceiro'.

studio_albums.title: Pirata
studio_albums.label: WEA (Warner)
studio_albums.notes: First part of 'Tetralogy of Elements'. Recorded live then reworked in studio. Marked shift toward harder rock.

studio_albums.title: El Diablo
studio_albums.label: CGD / East West
studio_albums.notes: Second part of 'Tetralogy of Elements' (Fire). Commercial breakthrough. Hard rock sound. Includes 'El Diablo', 'Tex', 'Proibito'.

studio_albums.title: Terremoto
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: Third part of 'Tetralogy of Elements' (Earth). Hard rock with social commentary. Includes 'Soldi', 'Dinosauro', 'Il mistero di Giulia'.

studio_albums.title: Spirito
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: Fourth part of 'Tetralogy of Elements' (Air). Lighter, more positive sound. Includes 'Spirito', 'Lacio Drom', 'Lo Spettacolo'.

studio_albums.title: Mondi Sommersi
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: Fifth part of 'Tetralogy of Elements' (Water). More experimental. Includes 'Maudit', 'Fata Morgana'.

studio_albums.title: Croce e Delizia
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: Last studio album with Piero Pelù (1st era). Pop-rock direction. Includes 'Croce e delizia'.

studio_albums.title: Infinito
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: Final album of the Pelù 1st era. Pop-oriented. Includes 'Il mio corpo che cambia', 'Vivere il mio tempo', 'Mascherina'.

studio_albums.title: Elettromacumba
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: First album with Gianluigi Cavallo. Latin/worldbeat influences. Includes 'Elettromacumba', 'Suona fratello'.

studio_albums.title: Insidia
studio_albums.label: EMI
studio_albums.notes: Second album with Cavallo. Darker, more introspective. Includes 'Insidia', 'Re del silenzio'.

studio_albums.title: Essere o Sembrare
studio_albums.label: Edel
studio_albums.notes: Third album with Cavallo. Mixed reception. Pop-rock sound. Includes 'Essere o sembrare'.

studio_albums.title: Grande Nazione
studio_albums.label: Rhino Records / Warner Music
studio_albums.notes: Second part of 'Trilogy of States'. Return to harder rock sound after reunion.

studio_albums.title: Eutòpia
studio_albums.label: T.E.G. / Warner Music
studio_albums.notes: Third part of 'Trilogy of States'. Final studio album. Includes 'Eutopia', 'La mia valigia'.

live_albums.label: CGD
live_albums.notes: Rare live album from 1984, later reissued.

record_labels.notes: First label partnership, later became part of East West/Warner.

record_labels.name: WEA (Warner Elektra Atlantic)
record_labels.notes: Most productive era. Released Trilogy of Power and Pirata.

florence_scene.description: Litfiba emerged from the Florentine underground music scene of the 1980s, centered around clubs like Rokkoteca Brighton, Manila, Faro, Casablanca. They were pioneers of Italian post-punk/new wave alongside other local acts.

italian_underground_network.description: Part of the broader Italian alternative rock/punk movement of the 1980s. Shared stages and audiences with punk and post-punk bands across Italy.

connections_detail.description: Both Florence-based new wave/post-punk bands. Litfiba and Diaframma shared stages and audiences. Tour dates in France were shared between the two bands. Miro Sassolini (Diaframma) and Piero Pelù performed 'Amsterdam' as a duet.
Both key bands of Italian 1980s alternative rock. CCCP was punk, Litfiba was new wave, but they shared the same underground ethos and audiences.
Florence band from the same underground scene. Ghigo Renzulli was briefly in Café Caracas before founding Litfiba.

trilogy_of_power.name: Trilogia del Potere
trilogy_of_power.theme: Critique of power, oppression, political corruption, and social injustice.

tetralogy_of_elements.name: Tetralogia degli Elementi
tetralogy_of_elements.theme: Symbolic journey representing the four classical elements.

trilogy_of_states.name: Trilogia degli Stati
trilogy_of_states.theme: Exploration of states of being, society, and utopia.

legacy.significance: One of the most important and influential Italian rock bands. Sold approximately 10 million records. Pioneered Italian-language rock music. Bridged underground/alternative scene with mainstream success.
achievements: First Italian rock band to sell out major stadiums
Pioneered Italian-language rock in a market dominated by English-language acts
Successfully transitioned from underground to mainstream without losing artistic credibility
One of few Italian bands to tour extensively in Europe
legacy.final_show: December 2022 - 'Ultimo Girone' farewell tour concluded with final concerts. Piero Pelù and Ghigo Renzulli announced the end of the band.
legacy.post_band: Ghigo Renzulli continues solo career. Piero Pelù continues with solo projects and occasional collaborations.
